extracted.intended_audience: State Exchange administrators and compliance staff; HHS program and audit staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for State Exchanges to participate in the State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) program, including sampling, review, appeals, corrective action plans, data protections, and compliance enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size calculated to estimate improper payment rate across all Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(a)(1), the sample size would be calculated to estimate an improper payment rate across all Exchanges using Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary statutory requirement is accurate improper payment measurement and reporting at a program level; national aggregate estimate is a key output.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific sample sizes based on overall APTC expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(a)(2)(i), sample sizes for each State Exchange would consider overall APTC expenditures; higher APTC expenditures generally warrant larger sample sizes because they represent greater financial risk and larger impact on national improper payment estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a State Exchange accounting for 20% of overall APTC payments would need a larger sample to meet precision goals and avoid undue uncertainty in national estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-level precision goals
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(a)(2)(ii), State-level precision goals would establish acceptable margins of error for State improper payment rate estimates; precision targets would balance statistical reliability with operational feasibility and could vary by State based on Exchange size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger Exchanges may be held to tighter precision standards; precision goals consider APTC volumes, available resources, and need for meaningful measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-cycle improper payment rates and variability inform sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(a)(2)(iii), the State Exchange's prior SEIPM improper payment rate and measurement variability would be considered; higher rates or high variability could require larger samples to achieve desired precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States with consistently low/stable rates could justify smaller samples to allocate resources efficiently; high variability or higher prior rates justify increased sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(a)(3), HHS would establish minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity while maintaining operational feasibility across Exchanges of varying sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design produces statistically valid estimates at aggregate and State levels, but recognizes State-level precision will vary with Exchange size and sample size; smaller Exchanges may have wider confidence intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling unit: tax household; annual random sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(b), HHS would select annual random samples of tax households from data provided by each State Exchange; the tax household is the sampling unit because it aggregates individuals for APTC purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the tax household ensures measurement is meaningful relative to APTC determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange notification contents for sampled records
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(c)(1), HHS would notify each State Exchange of (i) total number of sampled tax households, (ii) a unique identifier for each sampled tax household, and (iii) any instructions/requirements to facilitate HHS' review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification provides State Exchanges information necessary to gather and submit documentation and fosters efficient, accurate data submission under §155.1615(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All data exchanged during SEIPM would be protected under FISMA and HIPAA (45 CFR parts 160 and 164), use encryption protocols compliant with NIST SP 800-53 and ARS, and implement role-based access controls and continuous monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative, physical, and technical safeguards must ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronically protected health information; access restricted to authorized personnel only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampled records notification timeline (60 calendar days)
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(c)(2), HHS would provide the sampled records notification no later than 60 calendar days after receipt of universe data from all State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeframe accounts for coordination complexity across Exchanges, quality assurance review of sampling methodology, and balances thoroughness with timely completion of measurement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension procedures and required transparency for notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1620(c)(3), HHS could extend the 60-day timeline for specified circumstances (technical issues, data quality issues, other circumstances beyond HHS' control) and must notify affected Exchanges in writing of the extension, reason, and impact on subsequent SEIPM timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions limited to defined circumstances and require transparent communication to support planning and maintain accountability while preserving statistical integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized review criteria for record reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(a)(1), HHS would conduct comprehensive reviews using standardized review criteria designed to ensure consistency while accommodating allowable State-specific operational variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria designed to minimize reviewer variability; HHS will make a general overview of the review methodology available on the CMS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tax household information and consumer-submitted documents in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(a)(2), reviews would use tax household information provided under §155.1615(b)(3), including relevant consumer-submitted documents gathered by the State Exchange during enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures HHS reviews are based on the same information available to State Exchanges at the time of original APTC determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of errors that can result in improper APTC payments
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(a)(3), review would identify whether the State Exchange erred in: (i) enrolling or re-enrolling a consumer into a QHP for which APTC was paid; (ii) consumer eligibility for APTC; (iii) calculating the APTC amount paid; (iv) taking required actions upon changes affecting APTC eligibility or amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach aims to identify and measure all improper payment types related to APTC and support PIIA requirements and program integrity objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply consistent review standards anchored in existing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(a)(4), HHS would apply consistent review standards based on APTC determination requirements established in 45 CFR part 155, subparts D and E, and other applicable part 155 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchoring reviews in existing regulatory framework ensures errors are evaluated against established requirements rather than subjective program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to evaluate each identified error to determine improper payment amount
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(b), for each identified error HHS would: (1) calculate the correct APTC amount per section 36B of the IRC and implementing regs; (2) determine the improper APTC amount as the difference between paid and correct amounts; (3) document the error in a Sampled Unit Assessment Package and provide it to the State; (4) extrapolate identified improper payments from the sample to estimate the universe using statistically valid methodologies that comply with OMB Circular No. A-123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and extrapolation steps support transparency and statistically valid estimation of total improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of improper payment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1625(c), HHS would publish in the AFR: (1) an aggregate improper payment rate estimated across the FFE and all State Exchanges; and (2) an aggregate improper payment rate across all State Exchanges per 31 U.S.C. 3352(c)(1)(B), and would provide each State Exchange a State-specific improper payment rate and error analysis report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reporting ensures PIIA compliance and provides State-specific actionable data for corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Resolution (DR) request timing and filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(a)(1), a State Exchange may submit a written Difference Resolution request to HHS within 30 calendar days after issuance of a Sampled Unit Assessment Package to dispute HHS' error and improper payment findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-day window balances sufficient review time for States with administrative efficiency needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS procedures for reviewing Difference Resolution requests
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(a)(2), upon receipt of a DR request HHS would: (i) engage collaboratively with the State Exchange to examine disputed findings and additional documentation; (ii) evaluate disputes using the same protocol as the original review while considering new or existing evidence; (iii) prepare a Difference Resolution Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative process allows States to present context not available in initial assessment while maintaining consistent evaluation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for Difference Resolution Decision (90 calendar days)
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(a)(3), HHS would communicate the DR Decision to the State Exchange within 90 calendar days of receiving the written DR request and include a summary of analysis and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline balances thorough review of complex eligibility/payment determinations with need for timely resolution to support SEIPM cycle schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal filing window and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(b)(1), if DR does not resolve the finding, the State Exchange may request an administrative appeal in writing within 15 business days after issuance of the Difference Resolution Decision; new evidence generally not permitted though clarifying context is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter filing period reflects that the appeal builds on the established record; limitation on new evidence promotes finality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal adjudication procedures and decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(b)(2)-(3), HHS would assign qualified internal reviewers not part of the original review, conduct comprehensive review of the administrative record applying the same protocol, prepare a decision based on a preponderance of the evidence, and issue the decision within 90 calendar days of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of independent internal reviewers ensures objectivity; process is administrative (not a judicial proceeding) and decision must include analysis and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of Difference Resolution and appeal submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(c), all DR and appeal requests must contain: (1) clear statement of specific finding(s) challenged; (2) all factual and legal bases for the request; (3) evidence directly related to the findings, which may include clarifying data interpretation or legal citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured submission requirements ensure HHS has sufficient information for meaningful review and promote efficient dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of DR/appeal outcomes during and after SEIPM cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(d)(1)-(2), DRs or appeals resolved in favor of a State during the current SEIPM cycle will result in adjusted improper payment calculations and updated aggregate reporting; post-cycle favorable decisions that materially change aggregate rates will be reflected in amended AFRs or other reporting and States will be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-material post-cycle corrections may not trigger amendments; material changes require public amendment and notification to affected States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause extensions for DR/appeal timelines and non-timely decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1630(e), HHS may extend timelines for accepting DR/appeals or issuing decisions for good cause (examples: need for technical analysis, delays in receiving supplemental info, volume/complexity, unforeseen circumstances). HHS' failure to timely issue a decision does not indicate acceptance of the State's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions must be for legitimate causes; lack of timely decision is not an automatic win for State Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) discretionary requirement and standard reference
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1635, HHS may require a State Exchange to develop and submit a CAP to correct errors identified through SEIPM, using minimum requirements based on Appendix C to OMB Circular No. A-123, with future sub-regulatory guidance to further detail CAP requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAP standards expected to align with other improper payment programs (e.g., Medicaid CHIP PERM).

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP required error analysis and root cause identification
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1635(b)(1), a required CAP must include an error analysis reviewing causes, characteristics, and frequency of errors and determine specific programmatic causes and root improper payment causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should inform targeted corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP required corrective actions and measurable implementation details
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1635(b)(2)-(3), CAPs must identify corrective actions to address root causes and must include measurable milestones, accountability mechanisms, monitoring and validation of progress, documentation of implemented actions, and regular status updates. For each identified error CAP must include: (1) specific corrective action; (2) status; (3) scheduled/actual implementation date; (4) key personnel responsible; (5) plan for monitoring effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements support oversight, evaluation of effectiveness, and enable HHS to monitor progress; failure to include them can render a CAP unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP implementation schedule and reporting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1635(c), a State Exchange must develop and implement a CAP according to a schedule and regularly evaluate effectiveness; Exchanges must maintain communication with HHS and provide implementation updates at a frequency specified by HHS, but at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular evaluations and communications allow HHS to verify progress and ensure corrective actions address programmatic causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing to submit, implement, or provide acceptable CAP
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1635(d), if a State Exchange fails to submit a required CAP, submits an incomplete CAP, fails to implement a CAP, or submits a CAP found unacceptable after technical assistance, HHS may determine the State failed to substantially comply and take actions under §155.1650.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may use remedial measures to ensure program integrity and effectiveness when CAP obligations are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM preparation phase for new State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1640(a)-(b), any State Exchange in its first year of operation must participate in a 1-year SEIPM preparation phase prior to full SEIPM participation; to satisfy the phase Exchanges must (1) complete information submissions for up to 10 unique tax households addressing HHS-specified scenarios, (2) undergo the review procedures in §155.1625(a) and (b), and (3) participate in HHS technical assistance (training, system readiness, data quality validation, process improvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation phase is designed to familiarize new Exchanges with SEIPM processes and to test readiness before the first full measurement; HHS provides an annual 12-month schedule for completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing duplicate audit requirements via SEIPM participation
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1645, HHS proposes to minimize duplication between SEIPM and annual independent external programmatic audits under §155.1200(c) and (d); SEIPM participation would satisfy certain audit requirements related to subparts D and E that result in improper APTC payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-regulatory guidance would specify which programmatic audit requirements are satisfied through SEIPM to reduce duplicative burden while preserving audits for areas outside SEIPM scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle: classify payments as improper when documentation is inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1650(a), HHS would classify APTC payments as improper when a State Exchange fails to provide adequate documentation demonstrating payments were made in accordance with applicable Federal requirements; burden of providing supporting documentation rests with State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with PIIA standards which require classification as improper when documentation is insufficient to determine payment propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific criteria for determining failure to substantially comply with SEIPM
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1650(b)(1)-(5), HHS would determine failure to substantially comply if a State Exchange: (1) fails to submit required data/documentation within Annual Program Schedule timelines; (2) submits data/documentation incomplete, inaccurate, or in a format preventing effective review; (3) fails in CAP process; (4) has a pattern (>5 instances in a SEIPM cycle) of non-response within 30 calendar days to HHS requests for clarification/additional info; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria focus on substantial compliance failures that materially impact the integrity and effectiveness of SEIPM rather than minor technical violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to cure before remedial measures for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: At §155.1650(c), before implementing remedial measures HHS would provide written notice specifying the nature of noncompliance and potential consequences and allow the State Exchange a reasonable opportunity to cure or demonstrate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice-and-cure approach promotes collaborative problem-solving and affords States due process before enforcement action.
